Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at Example 1 (date=2025-04-15):

History shows a clear downtrend from 73.01 on 2025-03-28 down to 66.51 on 2025-04-14 (the forecast date). But then the true outcome shows a significant rally:

The model forecast at day 1 is 66.33, but true is 66.19 (close)
Day 5: Model 64.65, True 64.39 (model slightly too low)
Day 10: Model 64.13, True 66.55 (model significantly too low - ~3.4% error)
Day 15: Model 66.24, True 71.06 (model significantly too low - ~4.8% error)
Day 18: Model 68.39, True 73.41 (model too low)
Day 20: Model 67.23, True 72.33 (model too low)
Day 22: Model 65.29, True 70.99 (model too low)

Wait, let me look at this more carefully. The model appears to be under-predicting significantly in the latter half of the 30-day horizon. The true outcome shows a clear upward momentum that the model missed.

Looking at the history leading into this date:
- 18-day history: 73.01, 71.45, 71.52, 70.46, 70.83, 68.54, 68.80, 67.98, 69.86, 68.55, 66.06, 63.82, 62.84, 62.06, 60.94, 62.12, 64.82, 66.51

This shows a downtrend from 73.01 to 66.51 over 18 days. But then the true outcome shows:


The price dramatically reversed, jumping to 71.06 by day 15, breaking above previous levels. The model remained stuck at 66.24, completely missing the 4.8%+ upside. This indicates the model lacks the ability to capture sudden market reversals and momentum shifts.
